name: govtech
description: SYNTHETIC. A Singapore statutory board under MDDI that builds and runs Whole-of-Government digital services, cloud and cybersecurity. All figures are invented.

cfo.voice: formal and precise, British spelling, acronym-heavy, writes about the agency in the third person

lore.assertion: Under the 2018 cloud-first policy, most eligible systems moved to Government on Commercial Cloud. The mapping between legacy agency codes and the cloud data platform is still maintained by hand.

constrains.effect: A hand-maintained code mapping drifts, so reconciliation failures recur after each migration wave
Legacy and cloud agency codes are both in use and are not interchangeable

lore.assertion: Since the public sector data security reforms were completed, every document carries a security classification and a sensitivity marking, and data access is logged.

constrains.effect: Documents are marked, for example, OFFICIAL (CLOSED) and SENSITIVE NORMAL

lore.assertion: The agency keeps a full set of monthly governance papers, because statutory boards answer to their Board, their Minister, and the Auditor-General for every reporting commitment.

constrains.effect: The agency files a board paper every period
The agency files a exco update every period
The agency files a steering committee update every period
The agency files a major incident review every period
The agency files a post implementation review every period
The agency files a budget utilisation report every period
The agency files a cluster performance review every period
The agency files a finance committee paper every period
The agency files a audit observations response every period
The agency files a risk register update every period
The agency files a service status report every period
The agency files a ministerial update brief every period
The agency files a close readiness memo every period
The agency files a data quality review every period
The agency files a townhall brief every period
The agency files a management accounts commentary every period

sections.heading: Financial position
sections.purpose: Set out the agency's month against the approved budget, with the variance stated plainly and attributed. Formal register, British spelling, no promotional language.

sections.heading: Close and assurance
sections.purpose: Tell the Board whether the books closed on the committed date and whether the result was affected, in terms a director can repeat.

sections.heading: Matters for decision
sections.purpose: Name the one decision or watch item the Board should take away, and why it matters now. Open with what the Board is asked to note and decide.

filing.rationale: The Board receives a monthly paper on the agency's financial position and the assurance behind it.

sections.heading: In brief
sections.purpose: Three sentences for the executive committee: the result, the direction, and whether anything needs them.

sections.heading: Results for {{var:unit.name}}
sections.purpose: {{var:unit.name}}'s month in one argued paragraph, so its cluster head can find their own line quickly.

sections.heading: Operations
sections.purpose: What happened in operations that the committee should know, and what is already being done about it.

filing.rationale: ExCo takes a short monthly update, presented as slides at the meeting.

sections.heading: Status
sections.purpose: Give the steering committee the current status of the affected service in one paragraph, without technical detail.

sections.heading: Remediation
sections.purpose: Explain what the programme team is doing, what it fixes, and what remains open.

sections.heading: Ownership
sections.purpose: Say who owns the component and whether that ownership is settled; an unassigned owner is a finding.

filing.rationale: A steering committee oversees remediation of any incident that delayed the close.

sections.heading: Incident summary
sections.purpose: What failed, how much was affected, and what it stopped, for a reader who reads only this section.

sections.heading: Sequence of events
sections.purpose: The order of events, with the point at which the close was put at risk made explicit. Carry the sequence without clock times.

sections.heading: Root cause
sections.purpose: The confirmed cause, the hypothesis that was ruled out, and the condition that let the cause persist.

sections.heading: Corrective actions
sections.purpose: What will stop a recurrence, and why the previous similar incident did not.

filing.rationale: Every P2 incident that touches a statutory close receives a formal major incident review.

sections.heading: What was changed
sections.purpose: Describe the change that was put in, and the interim workaround it replaced.

sections.heading: Did it work
sections.purpose: Judge whether the change fixed the condition it was meant to fix, on the evidence given.

sections.heading: Lessons learnt
sections.purpose: State what the agency should do differently next time, in two or three plain points.

filing.rationale: A post-implementation review closes out every remediation that followed a major incident.

sections.heading: Overall utilisation
sections.purpose: Report how much of the approved budget the agency used in the month, and the gap to plan.

sections.heading: Utilisation for {{var:unit.name}}
sections.purpose: Report {{var:unit.name}}'s use of its budget against plan, and the reason for the gap, for its cluster finance partner.

filing.rationale: Finance tracks budget utilisation by cluster every month.

sections.heading: Performance of {{var:unit.name}}
sections.purpose: Argue {{var:unit.name}}'s month against plan in a business partner's commercial register.

sections.heading: Watch items
sections.purpose: Name what clusters should watch next period, if the measures warrant it.

filing.rationale: Each cluster receives a monthly performance review from its finance partner.

sections.heading: Observation
sections.purpose: State the audit observation plainly: what control did not operate and what it caused.

sections.heading: Management response
sections.purpose: Give management's response and the action already taken, in the register of a formal reply to an auditor.

sections.heading: Owner and status
sections.purpose: Name the owner of the action and say whether the ownership is settled.

filing.rationale: Internal Audit records every control failure that delays a close, with management's response.

sections.heading: Risks that moved
sections.purpose: Report which risks moved this month and why, for the Finance and Risk Committee.

sections.heading: Control risk
sections.purpose: Describe the control risk the month exposed and whether it is now owned.

filing.rationale: The risk register is updated monthly for the Finance and Risk Committee.

sections.heading: Service status
sections.purpose: Report the status of the affected service for service owners who depend on it.

sections.heading: Workaround in place
sections.purpose: Explain the workaround users should follow until the fix is complete.

filing.rationale: Service operations publishes a status report whenever a service the close depends on degrades.

sections.heading: Key message
sections.purpose: Give the Minister's office one clear message about the agency's month, in plain language a press secretary can reuse.

sections.heading: Delivery and assurance
sections.purpose: Say whether the agency met its reporting commitment and whether the result was affected. Do not raise operational detail.

filing.rationale: The Chief Executive sends a short monthly brief to the Minister's office.

sections.heading: Close timetable
sections.purpose: Tell finance teams the committed close date, any revision, and the current status.

sections.heading: Risks to the close
sections.purpose: Name what could still move the close, and what finance teams must do now.

filing.rationale: The Financial Controller issues a close readiness memo before every month-end close.

sections.heading: Records affected
sections.purpose: State how many records were affected and which downstream reports relied on them.

sections.heading: Cause and classification
sections.purpose: Classify the data quality failure and explain how it arose.

sections.heading: Ownership of reference data
sections.purpose: Say who owns the reference data behind the failure. An unowned table is a finding.

filing.rationale: The data platform team reviews every data quality failure that reaches a statutory report.

sections.heading: How the agency did
sections.purpose: Tell all staff how the agency did this month, in plain words and without jargon.

sections.heading: What happened in operations
sections.purpose: Explain to staff what went wrong in operations this month and what was fixed, without blame.

filing.rationale: The Chief Executive briefs all staff at a monthly town hall.

sections.heading: Group commentary
sections.purpose: Comment on the management accounts for the month, the way a reporting manager writes for the CFO's review.

sections.heading: Commentary for {{var:unit.name}}
sections.purpose: Comment on {{var:unit.name}}'s figures and the main driver of its variance.

filing.rationale: The reporting team writes commentary on the management accounts every month.

sections.heading: Margin position
sections.purpose: Report the agency's margin for the month against plan, for the Finance Committee, with the cause of any gap.

sections.heading: Measures to watch
sections.purpose: Name the measures the Finance Committee should watch next month, and why.

filing.rationale: The Finance Committee receives a short monthly paper on margin.

episode_text.event.close_started: {period} month-end close commenced; the finance orchestrator began the overnight sequence on the WOG Finance and Procurement System.
episode_text.event.pipeline_failed: The asset valuation pipeline failed. Agency asset and service charge balances could not be valued for the period.
episode_text.event.incident_opened: Service operations opened incident {incident_ref} at priority P2 against the asset valuation service.
episode_text.event.hypothesis_recorded: Initial triage attributed the failure to an overnight outage of the finance system.
episode_text.event.hypothesis_superseded: The finance system outage hypothesis was ruled out; system logs showed no interruption in the window.
episode_text.event.root_cause_confirmed: Root cause confirmed as a stale legacy-to-new agency code mapping, leaving {affected:,} records unmapped and unvaluable.
episode_text.event.workaround_applied: A manual agency code mapping override was applied so valuation could complete for the period.
episode_text.event.valuation_available: Asset valuation completed for {period} following the manual override.
episode_text.event.close_delayed: Final close was pushed by one business day and escalated to the Chief Financial Officer.
episode_text.event.control_failure_identified: Review established the underlying failure as a control failure: the agency code mapping table has no registered owner and no required reviewer.
episode_text.event.remediation_created: Two remediation tickets raised: automate the code mapping validation, and assign ownership of the mapping table with a mandatory reviewer.
episode_text.fact.cause: Stale legacy-to-new agency code mapping in the reference data register
episode_text.fact.workaround: Manual agency code mapping override applied to complete valuation for the period
episode_text.fact.remediation: One ticket automates code mapping validation; one assigns mapping table ownership with a mandatory reviewer

evaluation_text.q.direct.group_revenue: What was the agency's total revenue for {period}?
evaluation_text.q.direct.group_gross_profit: What was the agency's gross profit for {period}?
evaluation_text.q.direct.group_gross_margin: What was the agency's gross margin for {period}?
evaluation_text.q.direct.unit_revenue: What revenue did the {name} cluster report for {period}?
evaluation_text.q.numerical.revenue_vs_budget: By how much did the agency's revenue miss budget in {period}, in absolute terms and as a percentage?
evaluation_text.q.numerical.worst_unit_variance: Which cluster carried the {superlative} adverse {label} variance in {period}?
